title: fluctuations: no accumulation, seeded random numbers
purpose: Exercises the no-accumulation branch of `fluctuations` [@epsrmanual], which samples the number N of molecule centres in spheres of radius `rmax` placed at random positions in the box, the distribution of N - <N>, and the averages <N>, <N²> and S(0) = (<N²> - <N>²)/<N>, the long-wavelength limit of the structure factor, related to the isothermal compressibility [@hansenmcdonald2006], and the start of the generator from a saved `randomno.dat` state.
fortran: `fluctuations.f`: `run_fluctuations` (averages, S(0), list-directed real*8 output), `find_fluctuations` (random spheres, counting)
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. One sphere size, radius 7.5 Å, 1500 random centres (Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992]); the reference gives <N> = 29.26 molecules and S(0) = 0.803 for the last pass. For comparison, a uniform fluid of 600 molecules in 36,334 Å³ (0.0165 molecules/Å³) gives 29.2 molecules in such a sphere.
inputs: `single.FLUCTUATIONS.dat`: `nsize 40`, `nsumt -1`, `nsamples 1500`, `rmax 7.5`, initial `ntotal 20.0` and `nsqtotal 410.0`; `randomno.dat` copied from ex56; `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test.
verification: `repeat 2`. With `nsumt -1` (the nsumts < 0 branch) nothing is accumulated and nsumt stays -1; the given `ntotal`/`nsqtotal` are ignored because nsumt is 0 internally, so the reference `ntotal` (29.26) is the mean of the current pass only. `initran1` reads the saved state, and pass 2 continues from the state saved by pass 1. Compared after each pass: `single.FLUCTUATIONS.n01`, `single.FLUCTUATIONS.dat`, `randomno.dat`.
